subject: Residency assertion & ops playbook for Dedicated - FinTek
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintek.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fintek.io
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Hi Grace / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move to procurement we need a short, written confirmation on a few items specific to our Dedicated deployment:

- Region pinning: that our workloads and all customer data for the account will be pinned to us-east-1 (no automatic cross-region failover for primary data).
- Isolation: confirmation that the dedicated GPU pool and associated disks are logically isolated from other customers (naming conventions, network ACLs, project IDs).
- Backups & snapshots: whether backups are stored in-region or geo-replicated; retention defaults and how to request shorter retention.
- Deletion: documented erasure process and approximate SLA for complete wipe of customer data (including KV caches, persistent volumes, and backups).

I attached our compliance questionnaire (FinTek-SOC2-Q-2026.pdf) — items 7–12 are focused on data locality and deletion. We have an in-house audit starting Mar 2; if possible, please send a short ops playbook or confirmation that we can include in the audit packet.

Appreciate a plain-language confirmation we can forward to our compliance team.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Information Security
FinTek Solutions
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintek.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Hi Laura — thanks for the questionnaire. High-level answers below; we'll attach the operations playbook and a residency matrix for your packet. If any item needs a formal statement on letterhead I can route to Legal.

- Region pinning: confirmed. For Dedicated customers we support explicit region pinning at the account level. Your primary compute+storage will be constrained to us-east-1 unless you request multi-region DR (which is an opt-in paid add-on).
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools are tenant-isolated; namespaces, VPCs, and storage prefixes follow a customer-specific naming convention (example: ftk-prod-<account-id>-gpu). Network ACLs and IAM scopes are not shared across accounts.
- Backups: by default snapshots are taken in-region (us-east-1). Cross-region replication is off by default; we can enable a geo-replication policy but it's considered a DR feature and will replicate encrypted snapshots to a secondary region only with explicit customer consent.
- Deletion: we have a documented erasure workflow that targets live caches, primary volumes, and snapshot retention. Typical confirmation timelines: 
  * Live data wipe + volume reclamation: within 24 hours of request
  * Snapshot removal (in-region): 24–72 hours depending on snapshot counts
  * Cross-region replica purge (if enabled): up to 7 days due to async replication queues

Next steps I propose: 1) share the residency-matrix.xlsx and ops-playbook-dedicated.pdf, 2) sync with Rishi and Karthik on any technical clarifications, 3) if acceptable, I'll provide a short plain-language statement for procurement.

Attaching residency-matrix.xlsx for the audit packet.

Best,
Grace
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintek.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Laura — adding some technical specifics for the audit packet. Short version first, then a few low-level bullets you can paste into your questionnaire.

Short: Account-level placement policy = "REGION_PIN_US_EAST_1" enforced by the control plane at allocation time. All primary volumes and KV caches are allocated in the provisioned availability zones inside us-east-1. Backups are snapshot-based and stored in the customer-specific storage bucket with server-side encryption; cross-region replication is disabled by default.

Details (for questionnaire fields):
- Instance / GPU pool isolation: Dedicated pools are created as separate resource groups with unique project IDs (proj-ftk-<id>). No shared host tenancy.
- Storage prefixes & encryption: S3-like object prefixes use the account namespace (ftk-prod/<account-id>/snapshots/...). All snapshots are encrypted with a customer-specific CMK when requested; otherwise we use Redwood-managed keys with kms-region=us-east-1.
- KV caches: ephemeral by design; we persist carved checkpointed KV blobs only if checkpointing is enabled. Checkpoint blobs are tagged with account-id and placement-region metadata.
- Backup retention policy: default 30 days for snapshots; retention policy can be set per-bucket via the console or API. Shorter retention (e.g., 7 days) is supported and can be applied by submitting a request to account-ops.
- Deletion flow (summary): revoke access -> trigger live-wipe agent -> remove PVs -> delete snapshots -> purge bucket objects -> trigger object lifecycle GC -> confirm via audit-log entry. Audit-log entries include timestamps and actor IDs.

Reference: JIRA-SUP-4521 contains the background change that added region pin enforcement and audit logging for Dedicated. I'll link the playbook folder in the external doc link for your auditors.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintek.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Thanks Grace / Rishi — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our internal audit team:

1) If we enable cross-region replication for snapshots (for DR), will we retain the ability to request a permanent purge of those replicas? Audit requires a documented rollback/purge path.
2) For the 24 hour live-wipe SLA, can you confirm whether that includes zeroing ephemeral KV caches (not just deleting pointers) and whether Redwood will provide the audit-log proof of the wipe action?

Our timeline is tight — the auditors asked to see the ops-playbook and a signed affirmation that the account-level policy will remain pinned until we explicitly request a change. Will you be able to provide that in writing?

-Laura
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintek.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 12:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Laura — quick responses inline: 

1) Cross-region replicas: yes, replicas can be purged. Purge is an explicit, irreversible operation that must be approved by both the customer account owner and Redwood Ops. The purge pipeline runs as: mark replicas for purge -> validate retention holds -> enqueue purge job -> delete replica objects -> run GC -> record purge in immutable audit log. Estimated window: up to 7 days due to queue processing and safety holds. We will provide a purge certificate (signed) and an audit-log bundle after completion.

2) Live-wipe & KV caches: the live-wipe agent performs a secure overwrite (configurable; default is single-pass zeroing) on ephemeral storage and deletes KV blobs. For cryptographic data-at-rest (if you use a customer-managed CMK) we also offer crypto-erase options where key destruction renders data unrecoverable. Audit proof: the workflow emits an entry to our append-only audit service with timestamp, operator, and job-id. You can request the audit-log bundle via account-ops API or through your Redwood Console export.

I've attached the ops-playbook-dedicated.pdf which includes step-by-step runbooks and a sample purge certificate. Also attaching a small screenshot of the account region config UI (screenshot-region-config.png) that shows how the account flag is set.

If the auditors want a signed letter, Grace — I suggest we produce a short SLA addendum confirming account-level region pinning and the deletion/retention commitments; we can route that through Legal.

Regards,
Karthik
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency confirmation for Dedicated deployment (FinTek)

Laura — thanks for the questions and great catch on the audit artifacts. To summarize for procurement and your audit packet (plain language):

- Redwood will pin your Dedicated deployment to us-east-1 at the account level until you request a change in writing.
- Backups are stored in-region by default; cross-region replication is optional and requires explicit opt-in. If enabled, replicas can be purged via a documented process; purge completion certificates and audit logs will be provided.
- Deletion SLA: live wipe + PV reclamation within 24 hours; snapshots removed in 24–72 hours (7 days for cross-region purges). Audit-log proof and a purge certificate are available on completion.

I'll prepare a short SLA addendum and a plain-language confirmation letter for you — can we aim to have that ready by EOD Feb 20? Once you sign, we'll attach it to the contract packet.

I'll also drop the residency materials into the HubSpot company record and share the DocuSign link for the addendum.

Best,
Grace
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
